newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder president Fontaine to retire.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder president Fontaine to retire.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc said Thrusday that its president, John Fontaine, will retire from the company July 1.
Fontaine, who is 65, will be a consultant for the company and remain a director until the 1998 annual meeting, it said.

Fontaine was elected president of Knight-Ridder on July 21, 1995. He had been a partner in Hughes Hubbard & Reed, a New York law firm, since 1964 and was outside counsel to Knight-Ridder from 1980 until he jointed the company in 1987. He served in various executive positions before being named president.
Knight-Ridder chairman and chief executive officer Tony Ridder told shareholders at their annual meeting that the office of president will not be filled immediately when Fontaine leaves.
"Jack has been intimately associated with the company since 1974 when he was the key lawyer in the merger between Knight Newspapers and Ridder Publications," Ridder said.
"He was also an indispensable force in negotiating our deal with the Walt Disney Co (to buy four newspapers) in the largest newspaper acquisition in history.
Ridder was referring to an agreement announced April 4 in which Knight-Ridder would buy the Kansas City Star and three other dailies owned by ABC Inc, a division of Walt Disney, for $1.65 billion.

Knight-Ridder is an an international communications company engaged in newspaper publishing, business news and information services, electronic retrieval services, news, graphics and photo services and newsprint manufacturing. The company publishes 31 daily newspapers in the United States.
